trip.title: Japan Honeymoon
trip.notes: AUTOMATIC schematic route builder active: on every website visit, js/route-planner.js derives ordered legs from scheduled destinations plus trip.travel_anchors, preferring Shinkansen and rail where practical. Added nearby wishlist destinations (without a day) can be suggested into suitable not-overfull days; route_preference=alternative preserves optional venues unconnected. Provisional autumn 2027, late September / early October, exact dates and all flights/tickets unconfirmed. Hokkaido is days 3–6 between Tokyo and Kyoto, requiring flights Tokyo→Asahikawa and New Chitose→Osaka to preserve a relaxed 14-day schedule. Rail-first for Hokkaido intercity connections, Kyoto↔Osaka, Kyoto↔Himeji, Kyoto→Tokyo. Mount Asahidake access and Biei require ground transport. Hokkaido Shinkansen currently terminates at Shin-Hakodate-Hokuto, far short of Sapporo; all-train route is possible but uses substantially more time. Map legs are straight-line schematic symbols, never real service geometry or tickets. Day-by-day travel minutes are rough planning allowances, not actual timetables; on-site planner adds attraction durations, same-day local transfer estimates and a 45-minute break allowance and highlights overloaded days. Activity times and transport allowances may need revision when exact 2027 dates and bookings are known. Added provisional overnight bases for nights 1–13 and a reservation readiness checklist. These are proposed locations and unconfirmed booking tasks only, not confirmed hotels, tickets or reservations. Keep trip.stays and trip.booking_tasks current when plans change.

days.title: Arrive in Tokyo
days.description: Arrive, check in and recover from the international flight.
days.travel_note: Airport arrival formalities and transfer to a Tokyo hotel; arrival time unknown.

days.title: East Tokyo
days.description: Asakusa/Senso-ji and Cafe Capyba in Sumida (reservation dependent).
days.travel_note: Local Tokyo trains and walking between Asakusa and Sumida.

days.title: Fly to Hokkaido · Asahidake
days.description: Fly Tokyo Haneda → Asahikawa Airport; continue to Asahidake if arrival time and ropeway/weather permit. Stay in the Asahikawa/Biei area.
days.travel_note: Haneda airport procedures, flight to Asahikawa, and mountainous ground transfer; ropeway hours and weather may limit sightseeing.

days.title: Biei · Sapporo direction
days.description: Blue Pond and Biei scenery; continue to Asahikawa Station, then ride a JR limited express to Sapporo when convenient (check actual schedules).
days.travel_note: Biei/Blue Pond ground transport plus approximate Asahikawa–Sapporo limited-express journey.

days.title: Jozankei hot springs
days.description: Forest valley and a potential ryokan night in Jozankei. Suizantei is an unbooked lodging option.
days.travel_note: Sapporo–Jozankei transfer and local onsen-area movement.

days.title: Noboribetsu hot springs
days.description: Jigokudani and forest trails. Travel from the Sapporo area toward Noboribetsu by JR limited express, then local transport to the onsen district.
days.travel_note: Jozankei/Sapporo connection, limited express to Noboribetsu and local transit.

days.title: Fly to Osaka · Kyoto
days.description: JR train toward New Chitose Airport; fly to Osaka Itami (or a suitable Osaka airport), then transfer to Kyoto. Hokkaido Shinkansen does not yet reach Sapporo.
days.travel_note: New Chitose airport transfer and flight, Osaka airport arrival, onward Kyoto transfer.

days.title: Kyoto castles & Gion
days.description: Visit Nijo Castle / Ninomaru Palace, then explore Gion and try Hikiniku to Kome (reservation dependent).
days.travel_note: Local Kyoto transit for Nijo Castle and Gion.

days.title: Kibune · Northern Kyoto
days.description: Kifune Shrine and the Kurama/Kibune valley, allowing time for transit.
days.travel_note: Round-trip transport to the northern Kyoto Kibune/Kurama area.

days.title: Osaka day trip · Castle, bay & Dotonbori
days.description: From Kyoto take a train to Osaka Castle, then transit to the Tempozan harbor waterfront and finish at Dotonbori after dark; return to Kyoto by rail. Aquarium is an optional swap, not a required stop.
days.travel_note: Kyoto–Osaka return rail travel plus station access (between-stop transfers estimated separately).

days.title: Himeji Castle day trip
days.description: Take Shinkansen from Kyoto (direct where scheduled, otherwise transfer via Shin-Osaka) to Himeji Castle and Koko-en Garden, then return to Kyoto by rail. Optional alternative: Hikone Castle.
days.travel_note: Round-trip Kyoto–Himeji Shinkansen / connecting rail plus station access.

days.title: Shinkansen to Tokyo · Akihabara
days.description: Take Tokaido Shinkansen from Kyoto to Tokyo, then explore Jimbocho and Akihabara. Shinjuku nightlife is optional if time allows.
days.travel_note: Kyoto–Tokyo Tokaido Shinkansen and transfer to central Tokyo (between-stop transfers estimated separately).

days.title: West Tokyo · Ghibli, Nakano & Shibuya
days.description: Ghibli Museum timed entry, Nakano Broadway and Shibuya Crossing/Nintendo TOKYO later in the day. This is a full day; adjust around museum tickets.
days.travel_note: Local Tokyo trains and station access; between-stop transfers also estimated separately.

days.title: Depart Tokyo
days.description: Fly home; leave a generous airport transfer buffer.
days.travel_note: Tokyo hotel-to-airport journey and departure airport buffer, excluding international check-in guidance.

transport_policy.notes: Use Shinkansen for Kyoto↔Tokyo and Kyoto↔Himeji, regular trains Kyoto↔Osaka and on practical Hokkaido intercity connections. Flight exceptions: Tokyo Haneda→Asahikawa and New Chitose→Osaka Itami, avoiding very long rail transfer days. Shinkansen only reaches Shin-Hakodate-Hokuto in Hokkaido in 2027. All 2027 services/schedules must be verified.

travel_anchors.name: New Chitose Airport (CTS)
travel_anchors.notes: Airport rail station on the terminal B1 level; mapped railway line ends at the station, not runway center.

stays.note: First Tokyo base; choose a hotel with convenient airport and east-Tokyo transit access.
After Asahidake; stay closer to Biei if using a rental car or local shuttle.
Convenient JR hub for the following Hokkaido leg.
Potential first traditional hot-spring ryokan night. Alternative properties welcome.
Potential second onsen stay, conveniently paired with Hell Valley.
One Kyoto hotel for five nights; make Osaka and Himeji day trips rather than changing hotels.
Final Tokyo base; consider easy access to the departure airport.

booking_tasks.title: International flights to/from Tokyo
booking_tasks.notes: Dates and arrival/departure airports are not yet confirmed; coordinate Tokyo hotel nights once decided.

booking_tasks.title: Domestic flights: Tokyo → Asahikawa; New Chitose → Osaka
booking_tasks.notes: Check 2027 schedules after choosing the exact dates; the itinerary currently allows two domestic flights.

booking_tasks.title: Ghibli Museum timed-entry tickets
booking_tasks.notes: Tickets are advance-only. Confirm the current international release rules for your travel month; don't assume entry at the door.

booking_tasks.title: Choose and reserve a Jozankei ryokan
booking_tasks.notes: Optional honeymoon ryokan night; confirm bath type, meal plan, cancellation policy and transport.

booking_tasks.title: Choose and reserve a Noboribetsu onsen hotel
booking_tasks.notes: Optional hot-spring stay. Compare room options and whether you'd prefer two nights in one place.

booking_tasks.title: Cafe Capyba animal-café reservation
booking_tasks.notes: Advance booking and opening days may change; check the official booking window near your travel date.

booking_tasks.title: Hikiniku to Kome Kyoto dining
booking_tasks.notes: Check reservation/registration rules and closed days before deciding the Kyoto dining date.

booking_tasks.title: Kyoto → Tokyo Shinkansen seats
booking_tasks.notes: Choose preferred departure time once hotel and flight details are fixed; this is a rail-first leg.

booking_tasks.title: Choose and reserve special-occasion sushi omakase dinner(s)
booking_tasks.notes: Compare Sushi Ginza Onodera, Kyoto Sushi Gion Matsudaya, Sapporo Sushizen Honten, and Tokyo Sukiyabashi Jiro (main Ginza shop). Pick 1–2 or more depending on budget and dates; all are ALTERNATIVES, not extra mandatory dinners. Jiro is exceptionally difficult and overseas visitors must book through their own Tokyo hotel concierge; separate checklist item tracks that process. Verify 2027 opening days, booking windows, counter seats, menu prices, and cancellation rules. Casual sushi and onigiri are walk-in alternatives.

booking_tasks.title: Ask Tokyo hotel concierge about Sukiyabashi Jiro main-shop reservation
booking_tasks.notes: The Ginza main shop currently accepts overseas visitors' reservations only through the concierge of the hotel where they are staying. Availability is highly uncertain. Official omakase starts at ¥88,000 pp; ID rules and cancellation fees apply. Check with the hotel after selecting Tokyo accommodations and exact 2027 dates.

booking_tasks.title: Consider Miyamasou mountain kaiseki dinner or overnight in Hanase
booking_tasks.notes: A remote mountain dining inn, not central Kyoto. If selected, allow significant transport time or consider an overnight substitution. Bus route 32 about 1h40 and only two return trips per day (verify), or arrange vehicle transfer. Official Japanese price tiers list meals from ¥22,770 pp and stays from ¥75,900 pp including dinner/breakfast; English page displays higher course/package prices. Confirm booking conditions, pickup and return travel by phone.

booking_tasks.title: Compare HOSHINOYA Kyoto for a special Arashiyama overnight
booking_tasks.notes: Luxury riverside stay reached by a prearranged private boat; not convenient as a five-night Kyoto rail-trip base. Compare substituting one Kyoto hotel night instead of adding a 14th night. Confirm check-in, boat transfer/weather fallback, dining arrangements, 2027 price and cancellation conditions.

booking_tasks.title: Evaluate a Hakone overnight at Gora Kadan between Kyoto and Tokyo
booking_tasks.notes: A full Hakone stop could include Gora Kadan, Hakone Open-Air Museum and Ropeway, but would replace/rework the already overloaded Day 12 and possibly one Tokyo night. Check 2027 ryokan rooms, onsen choices, meals, luggage forwarding, transportation and total price; nothing booked.

booking_tasks.title: Check timed-entry tickets for teamLab Borderless, Azabudai Hills
booking_tasks.notes: Current Tokyo museum is Azabudai Hills, not the previous Odaiba location. Timed-entry prices vary by date, tickets can sell out and refund/change policies apply. Select trip day later before buying tickets.

booking_tasks.title: Decide whether to book sunset tickets for SHIBUYA SKY
booking_tasks.notes: A top sunset option near Shibuya Scramble but Day 13 is already busy. Once dates and daily route are sorted, book suitable timed-entry slots early; rooftop can close due to weather.

destinations.name: Hikiniku to Kome (Kyoto)
destinations.notes: Charcoal-grilled Japanese beef hamburg steaks with rice. Closed Wednesdays. Advance paid online registration or same-day in-person registration around 9 AM; book when Kyoto dates are decided.

destinations.name: Cafe Capyba (Hikifune)
destinations.notes: Capybara interaction café near Hikifune Station. Advance reservation required; bookings open 2 weeks ahead. Usually closed Wednesday and Thursday. Group with Tokyo sightseeing, potentially Sumida/Asakusa.

destinations.name: Kifune Shrine (Kibune Shrine)
destinations.notes: Scenic water-deity shrine north of central Kyoto, famous for red lantern-lined stone steps and forest setting. Allow substantial additional travel time from central Kyoto; consider combining with Kurama/Kibune area. Coordinates approximate; verify before final routing.

destinations.name: Takaragawa Onsen Osenkaku
destinations.address: 1899 Fujiwara, Minakami, Tone District, Gunma 379-1721, Japan
destinations.notes: Suggested one-night traditional ryokan stay, not booked. Riverside open-air baths; mixed bathing areas use provided bathing garments. From Tokyo take Joetsu Shinkansen to Jomo-Kogen (~70 min), then prebook overnight-guest shuttle or use local buses. Potential Tokyo-area excursion; do not assume it is directly en route to Kyoto. Confirm shuttle schedule, availability, bath policies and rates for travel dates.

destinations.name: Ghibli Museum, Mitaka
destinations.notes: Advance timed-entry ticket required; no tickets sold at museum. International ticket releases are typically on the 10th of the preceding month at 10:00 JST; verify current rules when dates are set. Pair with Inokashira Park/Kichijoji; west of central Tokyo, not near Sumida.

destinations.name: Akihabara Electric Town
destinations.notes: Retro Nintendo games, electronics, anime merchandise, miniature and figure shops. Half-day minimum.

destinations.name: Shinjuku sightseeing and nightlife
destinations.notes: Explore Omoide Yokocho, Kabukicho and Golden Gai in the evening. Pin represents Shinjuku Station area; individual stops can be added later.

destinations.name: Nakano Broadway
destinations.notes: Vintage anime, manga, collectibles and specialty hobby shops. Pair with Ghibli Museum/Mitaka if timing permits.

destinations.name: Jimbocho Book Town
destinations.notes: Used bookstores, specialty manga, art and illustration books. Convenient with Akihabara.

destinations.name: Senso-ji Temple (Asakusa)
destinations.notes: Historic Tokyo temple and Nakamise shopping street. Group with Cafe Capyba in Sumida.

destinations.name: Mount Asahidake / Daisetsuzan
destinations.notes: Alpine autumn colors often peak in September; weather, ropeway and trails can be affected by early snow. Requires substantial travel from Sapporo; consider Asahikawa/Biei base. Approximate mountain-area pin.

destinations.name: Shirogane Blue Pond
destinations.notes: Turquoise-blue pond and larches, often colorful in October. Combine with Biei countryside and nearby Shirogane Onsen.

destinations.name: Jozankei Onsen autumn valley
destinations.notes: Forested hot spring valley southwest of Sapporo, particularly attractive in early to mid October. Could be a one-night ryokan stop.

destinations.name: Noboribetsu Jigokudani (Hell Valley)
destinations.notes: Steaming volcanic valley and forest trails; pair with a Noboribetsu onsen overnight. Typical foliage mid to late October.

destinations.name: Lake Toya
destinations.notes: Caldera lake and lakeside onsen scenery. Could pair with Noboribetsu on a southwestern Hokkaido loop. Pin indicates lakeside town area.

destinations.name: Zaborin (Niseko)
destinations.notes: Luxury honeymoon splurge candidate, 1–2 nights; private onsen baths in suites. Not booked. Verify rates, availability, exact location and transport.

destinations.name: Dai-ichi Takimotokan
destinations.notes: Large traditional mineral bath complex near Hell Valley. One-night option; not booked.

destinations.name: Jozankei Daiichi Hotel Suizantei
destinations.notes: Upscale ryokan option in Jozankei autumn valley, 1–2 nights; not booked.

destinations.name: Shibuya & Scramble Crossing
destinations.notes: Explore the famous Scramble Crossing, Hachiko and Shibuya shopping streets. Pair with nearby Nintendo TOKYO at Shibuya PARCO. Late afternoon / evening best for atmosphere.

destinations.name: Nintendo TOKYO (Shibuya PARCO)
destinations.address: Shibuya PARCO 6F, 15-1 Udagawacho, Shibuya City, Tokyo
destinations.notes: Official Nintendo store on 6F of Shibuya PARCO, next to Pokemon Center Shibuya and other game/anime retailers. Easily combined with Shibuya Crossing. Visit timing and crowd controls TBD.

destinations.name: Dotonbori / Tombori Riverwalk
destinations.notes: Famous neon-lit canal promenade, Glico sign and Osaka street food. Ideal evening finish to a Kyoto-based Osaka day trip. Optional 20-minute Tombori river cruise.

destinations.name: Tempozan Harbor Village (Osaka Bay)
destinations.notes: Waterfront promenade, views over Osaka Bay, giant Ferris wheel, harbor cruises and nearby Kaiyukan aquarium. Osakako Station on Chuo Line. Allow additional 2–3h if entering aquarium.

destinations.name: Osaka Aquarium Kaiyukan
destinations.notes: Optional attraction inside Tempozan area; whale sharks and multi-story Pacific Ocean exhibits. Would require extra hours on Osaka day and possibly dropping another stop; left unscheduled.

destinations.name: Osaka Castle
destinations.notes: Famous historical castle site, reconstructed 1931 concrete keep containing Toyotomi Hideyoshi-era history museum, substantial original-looking stonework and moats, large park. Day 10 morning; allow time for transit to Tempozan.

destinations.name: Nijo Castle
destinations.notes: Historic Tokugawa shoguns' Kyoto residence; original palace buildings with nightingale floors, painted screens, moat and gardens. Day 8 before Gion/Hikiniku to Kome.

destinations.name: Himeji Castle
destinations.notes: UNESCO World Heritage original wooden castle, major Sengoku / early Edo fortifications. Recommended day trip from Kyoto; can combine with nearby Koko-en Garden. Day 11 is provisional and may be swapped for Hikone or a slower Kyoto day.

destinations.name: Hikone Castle (Lake Biwa)
destinations.notes: Alternative to Himeji day trip, nearer Kyoto on Lake Biwa. One of five original castle keeps classified as a National Treasure. Pair with Genkyuen Garden. Not scheduled to avoid overpacking day 11.

destinations.name: Sushi Ginza Onodera Souhonten
destinations.address: 5-14-14 Ginza, Chuo-ku, Tokyo 104-0061, Sanlit Ginza Building III B1F/2F
destinations.price_guide_jpy: Dinner approx ¥27,500+ per person, plus 10% service (2026 guide; reconfirm)
destinations.notes: TOKYO SPLURGE: polished Edomae omakase counter near Kabuki-za, multiple evening seatings; seafood sourced from Toyosu and Hokkaido. Day 2 after Asakusa / Sumida is our first dinner suggestion, using metro to Ginza; Day 12 is already too packed. Reserve counter seats; check current dinner course, add-on prices and cancellation policy. Location pin approximate; use official address for navigation. Alternative dining choice, not a scheduled stop.

destinations.name: Sushi Gion Matsudaya
destinations.price_guide_jpy: Dinner omakase around ¥41,800+ per person; menu and charges vary (2026)
destinations.notes: KYOTO SPLURGE: six-seat reservation-only Edomae counter in Gion, 17:00 or 19:30 seating; excellent special-occasion option in atmospheric old Kyoto. This would REPLACE Hikiniku to Kome dinner on day 8, or go on another Kyoto night, not be stacked on top. Strong cancellation terms; confirm final total and seafood allergy policies. Pin is approximate; navigate by official address.

destinations.name: Sushizen Honten (Maruyama)
destinations.price_guide_jpy: Omakase from ¥36,000 pp, plus 10% service; other courses from ¥16,500 (2026)
destinations.notes: HOKKAIDO SPLURGE: refined traditional Sapporo counter showcasing regional seafood. Best candidate after the Biei-to-Sapporo train day (day 4), only if arrival time permits. Dinner 17:30–21:30; closed Tue/Wed under current schedule. Explicitly request counter seating and confirm chef-led course; booking request is not confirmed until acceptance. Approximate location pin.

destinations.name: Nemuro Hanamaru (Sapporo Stellar Place)
destinations.address: JR Tower Stellar Place Center 6F, Kita 5-jo Nishi 4-chome, Chuo-ku, Sapporo 060-0005
destinations.price_guide_jpy: A la carte / conveyor-belt; pay by plates, verify current prices
destinations.notes: HOKKAIDO CASUAL PICK: energetic conveyor-belt sushi using Nemuro / eastern Hokkaido seafood, right at Sapporo Station; very convenient after a train arrival on day 4. Official hours 11:00–22:00 (last order 21:30) as of 2026; no table reservations, use the queue-ticket machine and expect a wait. Great alternative to Sushizen on the same evening. Approximate pin near JR Tower.

destinations.name: Sushi no Midori (Shibuya Mark City)
destinations.address: Shibuya Mark City East 4F, 1-12-3 Dogenzaka, Shibuya-ku, Tokyo 150-0043
destinations.price_guide_jpy: A la carte / sets, good value; check current menu
destinations.notes: TOKYO CASUAL PICK: classic sushi restaurant with generous nigiri portions and good value, connected to Shibuya Station. Fits after Shibuya / Nintendo TOKYO on day 13 ONLY if other stops are trimmed; this is already a packed day. Current hours 11:00–21:00 (last order 20:30); queue-ticket system can be busy. This is a dining alternative, not another mandatory stop. Approximate building-center pin.

destinations.name: Harukoma Sushi Honten
destinations.price_guide_jpy: Approx ¥2,500–5,000 pp, informal 2026 guide; check in person
destinations.notes: OSAKA HOLE-IN-THE-WALL PICK: compact, lively Tenjinbashisuji counter famous for generous cuts of fish, tuna and eel; queues and early sell-outs are common. Currently listed around 11:00–21:30, generally closed Tuesdays; confirm before travel. This requires a detour from day 10's Osaka Bay + Dotonbori route, so treat as a SUBSTITUTE dining destination, not an extra stop. Coordinates approx from restaurant guide.

destinations.name: Miyamasou (Hanase, Kyoto)
destinations.price_guide_jpy: Japanese official site: dinner/lunch ¥22,770 / ¥27,830 / ¥33,880 pp incl tax/service; overnight from ¥75,900 pp incl dinner + breakfast. English official page lists ¥33,880 dining and ¥88,550 overnight. Confirm available course/package and 2027 pricing.
destinations.notes: REMOTE HONEYMOON EXPERIENCE: historic mountain ryokan/restaurant specializing in tsumikusa (wild-foraged herbs, river fish, mountain produce and game) amid tranquil forests and streams in Hanase. Not sushi. Could replace part/all of northern Kyoto Day 9 or become a Kyoto-region overnight alternative; don't treat as an ordinary Gion dinner. Official public transport is Kyoto Bus 32 from Kitaoji or Demachiyanagi to Daihiyama (about 1h40 bus, only two round trips per day), plus access to the inn; discuss pickup/return and luggage with the property. If driving, inn recommends approach via Kurama Onsen (Route 38), not narrow Momoi Pass. Official Japanese and English pages list different price tiers; confirm the available 2027 meal and overnight packages. Dining and accommodation bookings by phone (+81 75-746-0231). Coordinates derived from mapped venue location. NOT BOOKED.

destinations.name: Sukiyabashi Jiro (Ginza Main Shop)
destinations.address: Tsukamoto Sogyo Building B1F, 4-2-15 Ginza, Chuo City, Tokyo 104-0061, Japan
destinations.price_guide_jpy: Chef omakase (~20 pieces) from ¥88,000 pp including tax; subject to the day's ingredients, as listed on official site 2026
destinations.notes: TOKYO BUCKET-LIST OMAKASE: original Jiro counter, Ginza (not the Roppongi branch), expertly prepared Edomae nigiri with formal, focused service. Overseas visitors must request a booking through the concierge of the HOTEL WHERE THEY ARE STAYING; direct reservations from overseas / unapproved booking proxies are not accepted. Photo ID may be required when booking and on arrival. Bookings are difficult and NOT guaranteed. Currently closed Sunday/public holidays and Saturday evenings. Official price starts ¥88,000 pp, with a ¥44,000 cancellation charge starting 7 days ahead. Proposed Day 2 as ALTERNATIVE to Sushi Ginza Onodera; verify exact day/time and 2027 pricing. NOT BOOKED.

destinations.name: Onigiri Bongo (Otsuka)
destinations.price_guide_jpy: Budget around ¥1,000–2,000 pp for onigiri and sides (2026 guide)
destinations.notes: CASUAL TOKYO FAVORITE: fluffy, generously filled hand-made rice balls from an institution with 50+ fillings, near JR Otsuka North Exit (2 min walk). Try egg yolk, sujiko/salmon roe or salmon fillings. Expect a potentially long walk-in counter queue; takeout orders by phone may be possible but online orders are not. 2026 hours commonly Mon–Sat 09:00–21:00, closed Sunday, verify. Could be a meal swap during west-Tokyo Day 13, which is already packed; not an extra required stop. Marker approximate; use street address.

destinations.name: Onigiri Asakusa Yadoroku
destinations.price_guide_jpy: Lunch sets from ¥814 for 2 onigiri + soup/pickles (current official menu; verify 2027)
destinations.notes: TRADITIONAL TOKYO RICE-BALL COUNTER: longstanding family-run shop just north of Senso-ji, excellent lunch choice after the temple on Day 2. Fresh rice, crisp Edomae nori and many carefully prepared fillings; not sushi. Walk-in only, limited seats and rice may sell out early. Lunch 11:30–14:00 (except Sunday); dinner generally 17:00–20:00 only Mon/Thu/Fri/Sat; cash only per official site. Coordinates from restaurant's embedded map. Great simple lunch alternative during Asakusa exploration, NOT BOOKED.

destinations.name: HOSHINOYA Kyoto (Arashiyama Riverside Ryokan)
destinations.notes: Luxury honeymoon riverside retreat in western Kyoto's Arashiyama gorge, reached by a private hotel boat from a waiting lounge near Togetsukyo Bridge. Boat waiting lounge: 60 Arashiyama Nakaoshitacho, distinct from the actual HOTEL pin upstream. The official property operates advance-arranged guest boats (typically first afternoon boat 14:30, last 17:45; weather/river can require private-car transfer). Nearby Arashiyama Bamboo Grove pairs geographically, but a stay here would replace one or more of our central Kyoto hotel nights—not add an extra hotel night to the 13-night plan. Confirm rates, availability, boat transfer, meal inclusions and check-in for 2027. The hotel-area coordinates are approximate. UNBOOKED.

destinations.name: Gora Kadan (Hakone Luxury Ryokan)
destinations.notes: High-end honeymoon ryokan with traditional hospitality, beautiful design and onsen in Gora, Hakone. Near Hakone Open-Air Museum and Hakone Tozan Railway; the inn offers pickup from Gora Station when contacted. Would work as a special Hakone overnight BETWEEN Kyoto and Tokyo (possibly around Day 12) only if we rework the already packed transfer day and existing Tokyo hotel block. Not a short Tokyo evening detour; don't count as a booked stay. Confirm suite/onsen bathing arrangements, meals, cancellation policy and 2027 prices. GPS sourced from Relais & Chateaux hotel listing. UNBOOKED.

destinations.name: Hakone Open-Air Museum (Chokoku-no-Mori)
destinations.price_guide_jpy: Adults ¥2,000 onsite or ¥1,800 online (2026 official guidance; verify 2027)
destinations.notes: Open-air modern sculpture garden set among Hakone's mountains with Picasso Pavilion, colorful stained-glass Symphonic Sculpture tower and outdoor art installations. Official hours 09:00–17:00 (last admission 16:30), typically open year-round. Roughly 2 minutes on foot from Chokoku-no-Mori Station on the Hakone Tozan railway. Excellent pairing with Gora Kadan and the Hakone Ropeway on a future dedicated Hakone day, NOT scheduled for Day 12 yet. Map coordinates from published museum location.

destinations.name: Arashiyama Bamboo Grove (Sagano Bamboo Forest)
destinations.price_guide_jpy: Public bamboo grove paths are generally free to visit
destinations.notes: Iconic Arashiyama bamboo paths west of central Kyoto, close to Tenryu-ji and HOSHINOYA Kyoto's river gorge area. The famous path is short, so the 75-minute estimate leaves room for wandering and crowds; early morning is preferable for photos and a quieter atmosphere. About 10 min walk from JR Saga-Arashiyama Station. Could anchor an alternative Arashiyama half-day instead of the current Kifune Day 9 plan; Kifune is in a different part of Kyoto and should not be assumed adjacent. Optional; not automatically included.

destinations.name: teamLab Borderless (Azabudai Hills)
destinations.address: Azabudai Hills Garden Plaza B, B1, 1-2-4 Azabudai, Minato-ku, Tokyo
destinations.price_guide_jpy: Adult timed-entry tickets from ¥3,400, dynamic pricing (2026 official; verify date)
destinations.notes: Immersive, ever-changing digital artwork at its PERMANENT Azabudai Hills location (not the old Odaiba site). Timed-entry advance tickets are recommended and may sell out; official vendor shows variable prices, date/time-specific tickets and restrictions on refunds. Enter at Garden Plaza B B1, around 2 min from Kamiyacho Station Exit 5. Consider swapping this into the lighter Tokyo Day 2 rather than overloading Days 12 or 13. Optional, tickets not booked.

destinations.name: SHIBUYA SKY (Shibuya Scramble Square)
destinations.address: Shibuya Scramble Square 14F, 45F, 46F and rooftop, 2-24-12 Shibuya, Shibuya-ku, Tokyo
destinations.price_guide_jpy: Online adults from ¥2,700 daytime or ¥3,400 15:00 onward (2026; confirm 2027)
destinations.notes: Spectacular 229 m rooftop city views directly above Shibuya Station and Scramble Crossing, especially near sunset. Book timed-entry tickets early for high-demand sunset slots. Rooftop access can close in adverse weather; indoor viewing may differ. Current hours approximately 10:00–22:30 with last admission 21:20. Near already planned Shibuya Scramble and Nintendo TOKYO on Day 13, but that day is already packed, so use as an alternative or rearrange later; not automatically scheduled.

destinations.name: Meiji Jingu Shrine (Harajuku / Yoyogi)
destinations.price_guide_jpy: Shrine grounds free; gardens and museum separately ticketed
destinations.notes: Grand forested Shinto shrine dedicated to Emperor Meiji and Empress Shoken, reached from Harajuku / Meiji-jingumae area. Official precinct opens at sunrise and closes around sunset: about 17:20 in September or 16:40 in October, so this is a DAYTIME stop, not a late Shibuya-nightlife activity. Nearby Harajuku and within Shibuya Ward, but not at Scramble Crossing itself. A future pairing with Shibuya Day 13 if time is made by moving other attractions.

destinations.name: Omoide Yokocho (Memory Lane, Shinjuku)
destinations.address: 1-2 Nishishinjuku, Shinjuku-ku, Tokyo (near Shinjuku Station West Exit)
destinations.notes: Atmospheric lantern-lit alley of tiny yakitori counters, izakaya and bars just by Shinjuku Station's west side. Some individual shops have very limited seating, set a cover charge or accept only cash; opening hours vary shop to shop. Sits right next to our already planned Shinjuku nightlife area on Day 12, so it could REPLACE part of Shinjuku wandering, not become another long extra activity on an overloaded travel day. Venue pin marks the neighborhood lane rather than any one restaurant.

destinations.name: Fushimi Inari Taisha (Torii Gates)
destinations.price_guide_jpy: Shrine grounds generally free to enter
destinations.notes: Famous Fushimi Inari complex with seemingly endless rows of vermilion torii gates winding uphill through the forest. You can do a short lower-shrine visit or hike much farther up Mount Inari; 2.5h allowance is a flexible middle-ground estimate. Open access to the shrine precinct, though individual buildings/stalls have hours. JR Inari Station on the Nara Line is right at the entrance (about 5 min from Kyoto Station); arrive early for fewer crowds. Could substitute into Day 8 or 9, rather than assuming a free slot on the already full itinerary.

destinations.name: Hakone Ropeway (via Owakudani)
destinations.address: Owakudani Station, 1251 Sengokuhara, Hakone-machi, Kanagawa (route: Sounzan–Owakudani–Ubako–Togendai)
destinations.notes: Scenic aerial gondolas link Sounzan, Owakudani, Ubako and Togendai on Lake Ashi; dramatic steaming volcanic terrain and potentially views of Mt Fuji on clear days. This ONE MAP PIN is at Owakudani Station, the signature central stop, not the entire multi-station route geometry. February–November service typically 09:00–17:00, subject to weather, volcanic gas, and maintenance suspensions. Gondola rides plus Owakudani sightseeing fit a Hakone overnight/day with Gora Kadan and the Open-Air Museum. Would require restructuring the Kyoto→Tokyo travel day; not scheduled.
